(Fetched via WebFetch text extraction — condensed by fetch tool; direct curl blocked. Times of Israel newsroom. ToI timestamp: October 17, 2026, 7:01 pm Israel time)
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sissi announced Saturday that Egypt would take necessary measures to defend Saudi Arabia if requested, prompting parliament to schedule an emergency session for Sunday.

Speaking at the Egyptian Military Academy graduation ceremony, Sissi stated: "It is inconceivable that we would allow Saudi Arabia, its security or stability to be harmed." He emphasized Egypt's readiness to act defensively rather than offensively.

The announcement comes amid escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including strikes on Riyadh's international airport and Saudi Aramco facilities. The Iran-aligned Houthis have also blockaded the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, disrupting energy exports and Red Sea shipping.

Sissi indicated parliamentary approval would be necessary, requesting "an emergency session be held so that it can give us that authorization if we are asked." Parliament subsequently announced a plenary session at 1 p.m. local time Sunday.

The conflict threatens both Saudi security and Egypt's economy. The Suez Canal lost approximately $11 billion in revenues since Houthis began targeting commercial vessels following Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack on Israel.

On Presidential Term Limits
Sissi, age 71, also announced he would not seek another term beyond 2030, calling the matter "completely settled." He stated the Egyptian constitution would remain unchanged and that the period until 2030 would focus on developing a new generation of leaders.
